virus noun

also viruses, viral, computer virus, there’s a virus going around, germ

modern

Traupman 66: vīrus percrēbrēscit, there is a virus going around

vīrus, vīrī n.

noun, second declension, neuter; no plural in classical use

a virus

The modern sense, taken by the sciences from Latin. Classically vīrus is slime, venom, poison, and a stench (Verg. G. 1.129, Lewis & Short); eighteenth-century doctors used it of the matter that carried smallpox (Morgan–Owens). Of a computer virus, the same word.

Other words

  • germen vīrōsum — a virus (a poisonous germ)

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. virus (with a query)

    Morgan–Owens’s tentative paraphrase, beside morbus vīrōsus and pathogonum; vīrōsus is classically slimy or foul-smelling.

  • germen, germinis n. — a germ

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 64

    Classically a sprout or offshoot (Lewis & Short); the sense “germ” is modern.

Examples

  • vīrus percrēbrēscit

    there is a virus going aroundTraupman 66
